round1.verdict: pass — The Setup section has no gap of its own. It fixes the ambient dimension $n$ (implicit in $\mathbb{R}^n$), takes $K \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ compact, and takes $f \colon K \to \mathbb{R}$ continuous; domain, codomain, compactness and continuity are all stated, and every object is quantified ("Let ... be ..."). Notation is standard and well-defined: since $K$ is compact and $f$ continuous, $|f|$ attains a finite maximum on $K$, so $\sup_K |f|$ is a well-defined real number. Minor, non-blocking remarks: the ambient space is only implicit in $\mathbb{R}^n$, and $K$'s nonemptiness is not stated (relevant only to the degenerate empty case, and harmless under the usual convention). The unproved claim $\sup_K|f| \le 1$ and any missing hypothesis on $f$ (e.g. a bound on $|f|$) lie in the "Main bound" section and are not gaps of Setup.

round2.verdict: fail — The claim $\sup_K |f| \le 1$ is not proved (the section consists of the claim plus "The proof is omitted": no argument, no citation, no appeal to any result in the draft), and more importantly it is false under the Setup hypotheses. Setup assumes only $K \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ compact and $f \colon K \to \mathbb{R}$ continuous; neither bounds $|f|$. Counterexample: take any nonempty compact $K$ (e.g. $K = \{0\} \subset \mathbb{R}$) and $f \equiv 2$. Then $f$ satisfies every Setup hypothesis, yet $\sup_K |f| = 2 > 1$. The scaling is decisive: for any admissible $f$ and any $c > 0$, $cf$ is also continuous on compact $K$ with $\sup_K |cf| = c \sup_K |f|$, so no nonzero bound can hold uniformly over the class Setup describes. Compactness plus continuity yield only that $\sup_K |f|$ is finite and attained (extreme value theorem), never a numerical bound such as 1. The claim becomes true only if an extra hypothesis is added — e.g. $|f| \le 1$ on $K$, or $\|f\|_\infty \le 1$ — but with that assumption the claim is a tautology and establishes nothing. Hence the section fails both substantively (false as stated) and formally (unproved assertion), and there is no result in the draft it could depend on.
gaps: False as stated: no hypothesis bounds $f$; Setup gives only compactness of $K$ and continuity of $f$.
Explicit counterexample: $K=\{0\}\subset\mathbb{R}$, $f\equiv 2$ satisfies Setup but $\sup_K|f| = 2 > 1$; likewise $f\equiv c$ for any $c>1$.
Scaling: $f \mapsto cf$ preserves both Setup hypotheses for every $c>0$, so no fixed numerical bound can hold for the stated class.
Missing hypothesis: an assumption such as $|f|\le 1$ on $K$ (or $\|f\|_\infty \le 1$) is required; with it the claim is a tautology, so the section proves nothing either way.
No proof: 'The proof is omitted' is an unproved assertion, with no argument, citation, or dependence on any result present in the draft.
Compactness and continuity (extreme value theorem) deliver only finiteness/attainment of $\sup_K|f|$, not the value $1$.
